messages:
james: FYI APAC-prod GPU pool failing to reach target capacity after this morning's firewall hardening. Nodes stuck in NodePending with `keystore: decrypt` and `s3:PutObject` errors. Anyone looking?

anya: saw alerts. can you share the node bootstrap logs and audit-exporter logs?

james: paste (sanitized):
``
[2026-04-02T09:02:11Z] node-bootstrap: keystore fetch error status=502 url=https://keystore.internal.redwood/api/v1/decrypt
[2026-04-02T09:02:11Z] audit-exporter: s3.PutObject AccessDenied batch=47
[2026-04-02T09:02:12Z] node-agent: sts:GetCallerIdentity timeout
```

lia: interesting. keystore + audit exporter + STS all failing -> likely egress block to AWS controlplane endpoints (sts, s3, kms). did the FW default deny rule go live this morning?

infra-bot: ChangeControl: FW-2026-APR-02 applied to apac-prod (default deny outbound from subnets). Owner: security-team.

sre-max: cost/ops note 1% of APAC warmpool nodes in pending/backoff since 09:00; we're holding 8 reserved GPUs idling. If unresolved by 2h we'll burn into next reserved billing band, estimate incremental cost ~$1.6k/hr.

anya: can we temporarily add allowlist entries for controlplane endpoints (sts, s3, kms) scoped to the keystore/exporter subnets? prefer FQDN-based egress to reduce blast radius.

james: we tried FQDN egress but our egress proxy requires IP allowlist; the proxy team is overloaded. current fastest option is to add specific CIDR egress to AWS controlplane ranges used by this account (e.g., 52.95.0.0/16) and a short lived rule.

lia: downside: broad IP ranges are noisy but acceptable for 30m emergency. Alternative: flip a per-cluster feature flag to route keystore calls to the regional fallback keystore in us-east while we fix firewall config. That would add latency but restore joins. thoughts?

sre-max: fallback to us-east will cause cross-region egress egress charges and slower startup; but it unblocks provisioning quickly. tradeoff: ~200ms per keystore call vs paying ~$1.6k/hr if we leave GPUs idle. fallback wins.

infra-bot: Deploybot: keystore-v1.9.1 can be configured with fallback endpoints. CLI: `deploy keystore --cluster apac-prod --env FallbackEndpoint=https://keystore.us-east.internal`.

anya: action plan: 1) add short-lived egress CIDR allow for keystore/audit subnets -> AWS controlplane (30m) (james) 2) if that's slow, flip keystore fallback to us-east (lia) 3) audit role and KMS policies review for missing statements (anya) 4) ensure S3 audit-exporter has temporary credential flow (sre-max) 5) post-incident audit backfill (james)

james: opening firewall change CHG-APAC-821 with expiry 30m. tagging security lead.

lia: I'm prepping the fallback deploy, will hold until rule exists for safety.

anya: scanning IAM diffs from last rotation: no KMS statement change detected. looks like rotation earlier was fine. this is purely egress.

infra-bot: Alert: S3 audit backlog > 1200 events. retention pressure on local buffer.

sre-max: start fallback now. lia, you can toggle the keystore flag; do it staged on 10% nodes first to validate.

lia: toggled fallback on 10% - joins progressing for those nodes. rolling to 50%.

james: firewall rule applied (CHG-APAC-821)  temporary allow 52.95.0.0/16 egress from 10.120.0.0/18. monitoring.

ops-bot: Incidentbot: NodeProvisioning alerts reduced at 2026-04-02T09:25:03Z.

sre-max: capacity ramping back, warm-pool join rate normalized. shutting down fallback deploy after stable for 10m to avoid cross-region charges.

anya: we'll open a follow-up ticket to replace CIDR allow with egress-proxy policy or FQDN-based egress and tighten KMS+STS S3 endpoints in firewall config. also need audit-exporter to drain backlog and verify no event loss.

james: filing postmortem and cost delta. recommend runbook change: block-default should include an emergency allowlist template for controlplane endpoints to avoid last-minute CIDR decisions.

lia: noted. will draft runbook patch and follow up with proxy team for FQDN solution.

sre-max: cost summary: approx 90 minutes of degraded join, avoided ~$2k immediate waste via fallback and the temporary CIDR rule. will include in postmortem.

james: thanks everyone. closing monitoring loop, will post the audit backfill status later. :white_check_mark:
